thread:
anna: Quick sync — thinking about adding a 'tiered cheap-variant' toggle in Console so product teams can opt low-tier traffic onto cheaper model variants automatically. Thoughts?

sam: +1 on the idea, but UX needs to make the tradeoffs explicit. folks forget that quality can drop.

kai: What do we want the default to be? conservative (only degrade short responses) or aggressive (all token-heavy calls)?

marta: Default should be off. Enable via a clear policy: percentage of traffic + token cap per request. show estimated cost delta upfront.

anna: Agreed on showing estimated cost delta. Proposal: allow 3 knobs — fallback_policy (off/canary/percent), cost_threshold_per_token (micro USD), and max_token_fallback_length.

sam: Love the knobs. UX question: Where to show historical impact? a per-route cost-savings chart?

kai: Per-route chart + example prompts that would trigger fallback. Also a small simulation button that runs recent traffic through the policy and shows expected delta.

marta: Simulation is key. Add a note about quality regressions and auto-rollback if eval set drop > X. People will want safe defaults.

anna: Implementation note: routing service already emits variant_decision telemetry (route, variant, reason, tokens). We'll need a console endpoint to aggregate and display "savings by tier" and "quality regressions by prompt set".

sam: Telemetry + how we charge: do we surface token-cost estimates based on actual model per-token rates? need mapping model->cost per token in Console.

kai: yes, we should surface the effective unit cost after quantization/variant selection. routing-bot: config check: detected existing enum values: fallback_policy={OFF,CANARY,PERCENT}, token_cost_field present in catalog.

marta: UX flows: 1) create policy (choose routes + scope by customer tier/region), 2) simulate against last 7 days, 3) opt-in (canary) or turn on for tier. Show rollback option.

anna: Edge cases: region affinity (latency-sensitive regions shouldn't fall back to remote cheap variants). Add region-exclusion in policy.

sam: Also quota interactions: if a customer is on token-quota, fallback might reduce tokens consumed but also change billing. Need billing note and per-route quota calculation.

kai: For quota calc, we can report 'expected tokens charged' vs 'tokens saved' in simulation. Also add a warning if fallback would exceed a given SLA (like median latency > threshold).

marta: Short messages for engineering: minimal console changes: new policy editor UI, simulation backend, telemetry aggregations, and help text. Backend changes: policy evaluation in routing service and billing collisions checks.

anna: Proposed acceptance criteria: - Policy can target tier+region - Simulation shows cost delta and token impact - Console shows historical savings and quality regression metric tied to selected eval set - Rollout controls (percent/canary/undo) present.

sam: Nits: use plain language labels: 'Lower-cost fallbacks' not 'cheap variant' in product copy. People react poorly to 'cheap'.

kai: Agree on copy. Also add a small inline info bubble explaining when fallback is appropriate.

marta: I'll draft the mockups and the sample language. Anna, can you coordinate with Billing and Trust to confirm how costs and audits should be shown?

anna: Yep — I'll ping billing and trust now. @routing-bot can you create a follow-up issue with the telemetry fields we need and link to this thread?

routing-bot: Created issue #PLAT-1894: "tiered-fallback-console-telemetry". includes fields: route_id, customer_tier, region, variant, reason, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_delta_estimate, eval_set_id.

sam: Thanks. Quick UX ask: include a tiny sample prompt toggler in simulation so PMs can confirm example responses with/without fallback. saves time.

anna: Good call. I'll fold that into the mock. Meeting in 30 to review designs.

marta: :thumbsup:

kai: one last thought — add an override API so platform teams can programmatically enable/disable per-customer. Might be handy for support flows.

anna: yup we should expose it. ok, see you in 30.
